name: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)
summary: Canalith repositioning is the primary treatment after confirming the affected canal and excluding central or vascular warning signs.

Use Dix-Hallpike or supine roll testing as appropriate.

mistakes: Treating dizziness without identifying the canal.
Doing repeated maneuvers despite no diagnostic fit.
Forcing cervical extension in a patient who cannot tolerate it.
education: Teach a home maneuver only after diagnosis and correct technique are established.
Explain warning signs that are not typical of BPPV.
escalation: Urgent medical evaluation for central neurological features or atypical persistent symptoms
